_readme: Phase 4 judgement input: modernization/4-architecture/waves.json. architect.py prints the computed wave_score per context first;
order the waves from it, then apply the hard constraints of skills/phases/04 §4 and record each one you applied in `constraints`.
Every context must be in exactly one wave, or in `retired` (with the ADR that retires it). `merged` maps a context into another's module.

waves.name: Shared kernel
waves.proves: the build pipeline, the structural lint, the traceability update and one golden-master harness on a pure function — before anything with a database

waves.name: Reference data + read-only
waves.proves: data migration, field maps, decoding, paging, one screen, one batch job — with no write risk. Deliberately boring.

constraints: <constraint applied and why, e.g. reference data first although its score is not the lowest>
wave1_exit: Migrated reference data with field-level reconciliation green (G4 evidence).
One screen and one batch job passing the golden-master harness.
A batch-window baseline captured from the legacy.
assumptions: Every throughput, scaling and availability score (no runtime statistics supplied).
